title: Tap dancing and the Hoofers Club
summary: He played piano for dancers at the Hoofers Club and learned to dance himself, which led to an off-Broadway show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x:
Q. Dancing
I was a tap dancer. I was very much in earnest. I tried everything to be in show business. They had a place called the Hoofers Club, the Rhythm club. And all the fellas used to meet down there, when they had nowhere else to go. Nothin' but dancers.

Round 132nd & 2nd Avenue, somewhere near there. I'd go down there to play the piano. That's why I was in the show downtown, the off-Broadway show, Cause I know how to play for dancers. Then I wind up learnin' how to dance myself. Cause I liked it. I could keep up with them pretty good. ... This must have been '38 or '39, yeah. Somewhere like that, dancein'.
But I was still playing piano -- playing at the piano. But I could understand, I could play for dancers good, and they liked the way I played.
